what_this_is_not: This compares the printed column labels and section headings only. It does not claim identical title text, identical note wording, identical number formatting or identical numbers; the numbers are the numeric anova twin's. R's print method takes a digits argument; the Julia show method has none, and that is not compared.

cases.r_source: test/fixtures/c1_behaviour_p1/r_anova_print.txt, header line (print.anova.gllvmTMB_multi at P1 on anova() of three nested Gaussian fits, d = 1, 2, 3)
cases.julia_source: show(io, MIME"text/plain"(), gllvm_anova(fits...; test = :chibar)) on Julia fits of the same data, header line, as produced by c1b_julia_anova_print in test/fixtures/c1_behaviour_p1/helpers.jl
cases.r_header_line: model d npar  logLik deviance df   LRT         test   p.value
cases.julia_header_line: model          d       npar     logLik   deviance         df        LRT       test    p.value
cases.note: The labels are the whitespace-separated tokens of the printed header line, in order. The numbers beneath them are not compared here; the numeric anova twin (model-comparison/anova.json) owns them.

cases.r_source: test/fixtures/c1_behaviour_p1/r_anova_print.txt, lines that are one capitalised word and a colon
cases.julia_source: the same show(...) text, same rule, as produced by c1b_julia_anova_print in test/fixtures/c1_behaviour_p1/helpers.jl
cases.note: Both printers follow the table with a Notes: section when a row carries a note (here, the chi-bar-square rank steps). The title lines differ by engine name (R: gllvmTMB fits; Julia: GLLVModels.jl fits) and the note texts are worded for each package; neither is compared.
